steps.text: Place the beef tongue in a slow cooker and cover with water. Add the onion slices, garlic, and bay leaf. Season with salt. Cover and cook on Low overnight or 8 hours. Remove the tongue and shred the meat into strands.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the tomatoes and peppers in the hot oil until softened on all sides. Remove the tomatoes and peppers in a blender, keeping the oil on the heat; season with salt. Blend briefly until still slightly chunky. Cook the diced onion in the skillet until translucent; stir in the tomato mixture. Cook another 5 to 6 minutes. Build the tacos by placing shredded tongue meat into a tortilla and spooning salsa over the meat.

raw_recipe.description: This is a really mouth-watering way of making tongue. It practically melts in your mouth. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: This recipe is simple, delicious, and easy to make. For those of you that have never made "tacos de lengua," make sure you peel off the outer layer of skin before you shred the meat!

This was my first time preparing this and it turned out phenomenal! I used beef bouillon and taco seasoning, in addition to the onion slices & garlic (used minced) & bay leaves. The flavors blended real well and no salt needed. Next time I will either just make on the stove or use the high setting on the crock pot. It wasn’t quite tender enough to easily shred & I cooked it on low for 10 hours. I transferred it to a pot and finished it off on the stove, about an hour or two, checking for doneness periodically. It ended up turning out great & shredded much easier afterwards. I was able to peel the tough layer of skin off no problem. The taste & consistency is very similar to pot roast, as others have said. Kept the meat warm in the crockpot set on low until it was ready to serve. All raves over here, even my daughter loved it. I will be making this again in the near future!!

Here is my variation:

I cook the tongue with garlic only in a regular pot for about 2 -3 hours.
Once shredded I fry (no oil needed!) the tongue on a pan and add salt to taste. 
I use chopped red onion that I marinate in lime juice at least two hours before eating.
Chopped cilantro is mandatory!
My hot sauce is made out of jalapeño peppers and tomatoes about 1:1 for mild 2:1 for spicy. I cook them and then blend thoroughly adding a little olive oil.
I always have flour tortillas and corn tortillas available.
Avocado is a wonderful addition to this taco. 

I still have to find the first person who do not love this tacos. I have fed them to "people who do not eat tongue" for a pleasant surprise!!

I have been wanting to try this recipe for ages. I bought a tongue at the local butcher here in New Zealand and cooked it as recommended in the recipe. I have made a few modifications however. After peeling the tongue (my dog LOVED the results of the peeling) I shredded the meat, placed it in a medium sized bowl and added the following ingredients: 1 can of kidney beans 1 can of hot kidney beans 2 tablespoons hot sauce 1 envelope of Old El Paso Taco Seasoning 1/8 cup of broth (the water the tongue was cooked in) as well as all of the onions from the pot. I mixed this really well and after sampling it for taste and 'hotness' it is in my fridge marinating until dinner time. It already tastes DIVINE. I'm not going to tell my 15 year old twins what its made of...because I know they will love it otherwise!! i

I always go to my favorite taco truck and order tacos de lengua and decided it was time for me to try to make these myself. Mission accomplished. I
made them for after church Sunday lunch and this is definitely a keeper. I put them in the slow cooker with all the spices and a some salt because I knew it would need it. We came home from church and the house smelled wonderful. After cooling the tongue and peeling the outer layer, I chopped it up and before putting it in the taco, I sauteed it in a little bit of oil and sprinkled it with some house seasoning (garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper) and put it on my corn tortilla. I also chopped up an onion and cilantro and squeezed it with lemon juice (because I didn't have a lime) and let it sit for a bit. The citrus is really a must and really enhances the flavor. For the sauce I used a poblano pepper instead of the serrano but only because I bought the wrong kind and it was still good but it didnt have the kick that I like so I will see if the serrano are hotter the next time I make it. My hubby when he saw the tongue was grossed out but he tried it anyway and LOVED IT!!! We also had a friend over who thought it was lamb. We devoured every bit of it. And guess what's on the menu this Sunday after church? Tongue Tacos!! P.S. The kids ate it too!

I used jalapeño peppers and added some salt and pepper. Reminded me of my trips to Mexico. I blended the peppers and tomatoes in the food processor. Added A good squeeze of lime and some cilantro to top it off. Very easy and taste great!
Delish. Keeper. Instead of cooking the tomatoes, peppers, and onions, I chopped them up by hand and added a handful of cilantro and a squeeze of lime to make salsa and serve with the tacos.

This tasted just like a real Mexican restaurant! I was skeptical of beef tongue, but a friend gave me one, so I tried this recipe. I added some dried oregano and a little bit of cumin and chili powder at the end. I cooked it in the crockpot for about 7 hours on high. The salsa is really good too (I substituted jalapenos for serranos and deseeded first).

This is a great recipe that I've used multiple times. For those of you giving poor reviews saying it lacks salt, you do realize the recipe says "salt to taste", right??!? So who's at fault is it if it's not salty enough? Think about it and you'll get it right after you hear the loud popping sound. I also recommend adding beer, chili powder, cumin, red pepper flakes or even jalapeno or serrano peppers to the slow cooker if you like more intense flavors or more heat. Also, be sure to remove the skin after slow cooking and you can also sear/brown the meat in a skillet (after shredding) to give even more flavor.

I had never cooked or eaten tongue before so this was certainly a new experience for me. This recipe is simple, easy to make and delicious. The only thing I would add to the recipe is to peel off the outer layer of skin on the tongue before shredding the meat; otherwise, this becomes an extremely difficult task to accomplish. The flavor was great; much better than I expected. I will definitely be making this dish again.

I cooked the tongue for about 10 hours, shredded it, cooked the tomatoes and 1 jalapeno, then just threw the onion and meat in and cooked it altogether. It was wet, but the best tongue taco's I've ever had and everyone else who was willing to try it, raved!
Im making this today

absolutely delish. fully chased my teen sons around the house first before putting it in the crockpot. promise it made it taste better with laughter infusion. teenage sons said they wanted tacos for our christmas day meal so in it goes tonight! now this is a taco:)

Wow! Just wow!! When we took our first cow to the butcher, I made sure we got her tongue back. We had tried smoked beef tongue in the past so we were excited to see what else could be done. I followed this recipe & it’s now my favorite beef tongue recipe. I saved the liquid after we cooked the tongue & made a killer soup (best beef stock ever).
Mouth watering. Fell apart so tender.

This was the first time I’ve ever made tongue. I used this recipe for cooking the tongue, and it was fantastic! It was incredibly tender and tasted much like roast beef. We bought pico de gallo, so I can’t attest to the tomato/Serrano part of the recipe, but I’ll definitely use this recipe again.
Perfect just like it is! Easy delicious recipe I will be using again. Thanks for sharing.
I made it for the first time ,man it was so good . I love it & so did my grandkids .
Meat was extremely bland, and nowhere near as tender as I'd hoped. I won't be making these again.
Tried this for the first time but used oregano instead of bay leaves. ..cooked it over night and it came out soooo good everyone loved it....
